title: What would you pay for {product}? A 3-minute pricing survey
description: A short research survey about pricing for {product}. There are no right answers; we want your honest sense of value.
audience: People who choose or pay for tools like {product}, for themselves or their team
purpose: Set the launch price range for {product} using the Van Westendorp price sensitivity meter, segmented by current spend and who pays

welcome.title: What would you pay for {product}?
welcome.description:
We're the {team} at {company}. We're setting the price for {product} and want it to be fair to people like you. There are no right or wrong answers.
• Takes about 3 minutes
• Anonymous: only the {team} sees answers, in summary
• Taking part is voluntary; you can stop at any time
• Open until {date}. Questions? {contact}

thank_you.title: Thank you, that's everything
thank_you.description: Your answers will directly shape the price we launch with. We'll share the outcome within a month of {date}. Questions? {contact}

questions.label: Do you choose or pay for tools like {product}, for yourself or for a team?
What do you use today for the job {product} does?
Roughly how much do you pay for it today, per month?
questions.description: In {currency} per month. A rough figure is fine.

questions.label: How satisfied or dissatisfied are you with what you use today?
About {product}
questions.description: {product_description} The next four questions ask what you would expect to pay for it, in {currency} per month. Answer with the first figure that comes to mind.

questions.label: At what monthly price would {product} be so cheap that you'd doubt its quality?
At what monthly price would {product} be a bargain, a great buy for the money?
At what monthly price would {product} start to feel expensive, so you'd think twice before buying?
At what monthly price would {product} be so expensive that you wouldn't consider buying it?
Based on the description, how interested are you in trying {product}?
Who usually pays for tools like this?
How many people work at your organisation?
questions.description: So we can see whether price expectations differ by organisation size.
